newsitem.title: USA: Conn. residents favor property tax cut - poll.
newsitem.headline: Conn. residents favor property tax cut - poll.

text.p: Connecticut residents would rather see cuts in their property taxes than in their income taxes, according to a Hartford Courant poll published Tuesday.
The newspaper's telephone poll showed that, given a choice of cutting one or the other, 53 percent would want their property taxes reduced while 30 percent would prefer a cut in their income taxes.
The survey queried 500 randomly selected adults between April 2 and 9.
Deciding which tax to cut is one of the most controversial questions facing Republican Gov. John Rowland in the current legislative session.
Rowland has said he wants to slash the income tax, while Democrats -- who control both chambers of the legislature -- favor cutting the property tax.
The poll's results differ sharply from a survey a few months ago, poll director G. Donald Ferree said.
When the same question was asked in late January, 39 percent of those polled said they would rather cut the income tax, while 36 percent said they would cut the property tax.
